messages.subject: summarize_all() and approx()
parts:
Dear all

I'm trying to get summarize_all() to work with approx(). More concrete,
the data frame df is to be interpolated to height_target:

library(tidyverse)
df <- tibble(height = c(0, 10, 20),
a = c(1, 3, 5),
b = c(4, 6, 8))
height_target <- c(5, 15)

For the a column, the commands works like this:

approx(x = df$height, y = df$a, xout = height_target)

I was able to wrap it with summarize, which produces what I want but
only for one column:

summarize(df, h = list(height_target)
a = list(approx(x = height, y = a, xout = height_target)$y)) %>%
unnest()

To apply it to all columns, I would do something like

summarize_all(df,
funs(list(approx(x = height, y = ., xout = height_target)$y))
)

This, however, gives the error
> Error in summarise_impl(.data, dots) :
> Evaluation error: 'x' and 'y' lengths differ.

Could you please point me to the error?

Thanks a lot
Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: summarize_all() and approx()
parts:
Using `.` in place of y is throwing an error because `.` is a dataframe and not the same length as .$height. This error makes sense, but I don't know how to get around it. 

I couldn't crack it with summarise_all() so I went a different way using purrrrrrr

library(tidyverse)
df <- tibble(height = c(0, 10, 20),
             a = c(1, 3, 5),
             b = c(4, 6, 8))

height_target <- data.frame(height = c(5, 15)) # put this in a dataframe with the label height for predict later


gather(df, type, value, -height) %>% # gather up the different columns that you want to summarize
group_by(type) %>%   # groupt by the type 
nest(-type, .key = data) %>% # nest these datasets, but keep the label type
mutate(model = map(data, function(d) lm(value~height, data = d)), # compute the linear model (this is what approx does I believe)
pred = map(model, function(p) data.frame(height = height_target, prediction = predict(p, height_target))) # predict the values for each based upon their linear model at each point in height_target
) %>%
select(type, pred) %>% # select out these columns because they are compatible lengths for unnest()
unnest() # unwind everything again, you have type, height value from height_target, and predicted value at each target

Hopefully the steps are explained well enough in comments. I'm only just getting my head around map and its kin so there may be a way more efficient way to do this, but I couldn't come up with a way to use approx without the name of the column. 

HTH,

B

really sure whether the error

funs(list(approx(x = height, y = ., xout = height_target)$y))

parts: Hi all

> I'm trying to get summarize_all() to work with approx(). More concrete,
> the data frame df is to be interpolated to height_target:
>
> library(tidyverse)
> df <- tibble(height = c(0, 10, 20),
> a = c(1, 3, 5),
> b = c(4, 6, 8))
> height_target <- c(5, 15)
>
> For the a column, the commands works like this:
>
> approx(x = df$height, y = df$a, xout = height_target)
>

> To apply it to all columns, I would do something like
>
> summarize_all(df,
> funs(list(approx(x = height, y = ., xout = height_target)$y))
> )
>
> This, however, gives the error
>> Error in summarise_impl(.data, dots) :
>> Evaluation error: 'x' and 'y' lengths differ.

In a discussion on https://stackoverflow.com/q/45409032/1463740 , I
found the error: The problem is that the interpolation creates a new
column height first which is then used for the interpolation of the
other columns. Due to the different vector lengths, this cannot work.
Thus, height has to be identified directly:

df %>%
summarise_all(funs(list(approx(x = df$height, y = ., xout =
height_target)$y))) %>%
unnest()

Cheers
Sebastian
